title: Make a Paper Telescope
description: Turn a cardboard tube into a telescope fit for a stargazer. Decorate it, take it outside with an adult, and look at the Moon — never at the Sun.

body.heading: Build it
paragraphs: Take a cardboard tube from a kitchen roll. Wrap it in coloured paper and tape the paper in place. Add stars, stripes, or your name in stickers. If you like, tape a piece of string to each side so you can wear it around your neck like a real explorer.
Hold the tube up to one eye and close the other eye. Everything looks closer — and much more exciting. Your telescope is ready for its first mission.

body.heading: Use it kindly
paragraphs: Take your telescope outside with an adult, in the daytime or at dusk. Look at birds in a tree, clouds in the sky, or the Moon when it is out. Talk about what you can see: what shape is the Moon tonight? Is it a smile, a half, or a big round ball?

One rule never changes: never look at the Sun through your telescope, or with your bare eyes either. The Sun is far too bright and can hurt your eyes. The Moon, the clouds, and the birds are the best things to spy.

takeaway: A cardboard tube and a little imagination are all a stargazer needs.
materials: A cardboard tube from a kitchen roll
Sticky tape and a piece of string (optional)
supervision: An adult helps with taping and cutting, and always comes along for outdoor looking.
safetyNotes: Never look at the Sun through the telescope — or with bare eyes
An adult handles any cutting; the child uses child-safe scissors only
Stay with your adult when looking outside, especially after dark
